raṭṭhapāla.notes: The verses Raṭṭhapāla recites at his father's house are in MN 82.25 and Thag 16.4. The entry's MN.i.64f points to MN 11 in error. MN 81 is the preceding Ghaṭikāra discourse. The distinction for going forth out of faith is at AN 1.210, within the middle of the three cited AN ranges.

revata.notes: AN 1.203 names Revata Khadiravaniya for forest dwelling. AN 1.204 names Kaṅkhārevata for meditation. The latter also appears by his full name in Thag 1.3 and Ud 5.7, to which the summary in Ud 5.10 refers. MN 118 gives only the bare name. The acacia-wood elder's verse to Cālā and the others is Thag 1.42. The cited Thag 1.43 belongs to Sumaṅgala. Thag 1.42 and 14.1 both sign with the compound Khadiravaniyarevato.

reṇu.notes: DN 19.29 calls Reṇu Disampati's son. He succeeds his father at 34.2, keeps the central kingdom at 36.2, and is named among the seven Bhāratas at 36.15–16. Both DPD lines describe the same king.

rohitassa.notes: AN 4.45 and SN 2.26 give Rohitassa as the name of both the visiting god and the seer he once was. Both texts give the stride from the eastern ocean to the western. DPPN reverses the direction. AN 4.46 retells the visit, and AN 4.50's closing summary indexes the two accounts. AN 4.43–44 and SN 2.25 are adjacent citations. The Rohitassas of SN 15.20 are a people.

rohitassā.notes: SN 15.20.3 names the people of Mount Vaṅkaka in Koṇāgamana's time. Rohitassāpare duve at AN 4.50:13.2 indexes the two discourses about the god Rohitassa (AN 4.45–46).

roruka.notes: DN 19:36.6 explicitly pairs Roruka with the Sovīras. Bharata appears in the following list of kings, where the connection to his city is implicit.

roruva.notes: Kokanadā names the hell at SN 1.39:4.3. SN 1.40 gives the younger Kokanadā's verses on another subject.

rādha.notes: The DPD hint SN 22.7 appears to mean SN 22.71, where Rādha questions the Buddha and becomes an arahant. SN 22.159 features Ānanda. The distinction is at AN 1.233. Sujato reads it as inspiring eloquent teachings, while DPPN also suggests extemporaneous speech by Rādha himself.

rāhu.notes: The moon and sun seizures are in SN 2.9–10. SN 2.8, AN 4.14, AN 4.16 and AN 5.198 are adjacent citations. DN 20:12.12 names Rāhubhadda in a joined form. Snp 3.4:17.2 uses rāhuggahaṇā for an eclipse, and MN 13:14.3 uses rāhumukha as the name of a punishment.

rāhula.notes: Rāhula calls himself the Buddha's son at Thag 4.8:1.3. His distinction for wanting to train is at AN 1.209, within the middle of the three cited AN ranges.

rājagaha.notes: DN 19:1.2 names Rājagaha in the setting. The seven cities laid out by the Great Steward at DN 19:36.3–10 omit Rājagaha, so that list alone cannot establish the city's founding.

rājakārāma.notes: Nandaka goes to the Royal Monastery to instruct the nuns in MN 146. SN 55.11 opens there. The adjacent SN 55.10 concerns people who died at Ñātika.

sabbamitta.notes: DN 14:1.11.6 names Kassapa's chief attendant. Thag 2.15 signs the elder's verses, and the chapter summary at Thag 2.20:3.3 lists that elder between Somamitta and Kāḷa. At Thag 14.1:4.1 Revata calls himself a friend to all (sabbamitto sabbasakho).

sabhiya.notes: Thag 4.3 attributes its verses to Sabhiya, and Snp 3.6 describes a wanderer of that name attaining arahantship. Neither gives him the name Kaccāna. SN 44.11 names Sabhiya Kaccāna at Ñātika. MN 127 also gives the full name when he speaks to Anuruddha. DPPN treats his identity with the verse elder as conjectural. SN 44.10 is Vacchagotta's conversation with the Buddha.

saccaka.notes: MN 35 and MN 36 call Saccaka nigaṇṭhaputta and address him as Aggivessana. DPPN says that he became a follower after the meal. MN 35 ends with their exchange about the merit of his gift and records no declaration of discipleship.

sahadhammā.notes: Sujato reads Sahadhammas in the plural at DN 20:15.5, in agreement with the candidate and the DPD gloss. DPD flags a singular reading in the commentary.

sahajāti.notes: AN 10.24 and AN 10.85 both place Mahācunda at Sahajāti among the Cetīs. Two further settings translated as Sahajāti have variant Pali forms, sayaṁjātiyaṁ at AN 6.46:1.2 and sahañcanike at SN 56.30:1.1, where Gavampati speaks. SN 56.29 is the preceding discourse.

sahali.notes: SN 2.30:3.1 identifies the godling who speaks about Makkhali Gosāla. SN 2.29 concerns Susīma. DN 20:14.1 is translated as a group of Sahalī gods, with no detail identifying the individual disciple.

sahampati.notes: SN 6.1 and MN 26 give Sahampati's request to teach. DN 16:6.10.2 joins the title and name as brahmāsahampati in the verse attribution at the Buddha's death. The reverence episode is at AN 4.21. AN 4.9–10 and the adjacent SN 6.14, SN 11.15–16, SN 47.17 and SN 48.58 do not name him.

sajjha.notes: AN 9.8 names Sajjha at Vulture's Peak. The visitor in AN 9.7 is Sutavā. AN 9.10:2.3 lists both wanderers in the chapter summary.
